name: Ramp / Big Mana
summary: Land ramp, mana rocks, and mana dorks that build to a critical mass, then close with oversized threats or cheat them into play. Absorbs eldrazi-colorless as a sub-recipe.
_status_note: Live recipe — Gate 3 approved 2026-05-14 by local-board via interaction dec259-gate3. 17/17 = 100% canon recall validated empirically against Scryfall API.

basic_land_ramp.intent: Sorceries that search for basic land cards and put one or more onto the battlefield (the core green ramp package).
queries: f:commander t:sorcery o:"search your library for" o:"basic land" o:"put" o:"onto the battlefield"

canon_recall.sample_noise: Also surfaces Migration Path, Explosive Vegetation, Search for Tomorrow, Grow from the Ashes — all legitimate ramp, low noise.

forest_fetch_sorceries.intent: Sorceries that search for Forest cards (including non-basics) and put them onto the battlefield — the premium 2-drop ramp package.
queries: f:commander (t:sorcery or t:instant) o:"search your library for" o:"forest" o:"battlefield"

canon_recall.sample_noise: Also surfaces Nissa's Pilgrimage (basic Forest only), Ranger's Path, Hunting Wilds — all ramp variants, low noise.

creature_sac_ramp.intent: Creatures that sacrifice themselves to search for a basic land — repeatable-ish ramp that also serves as a blocker.
queries: f:commander t:creature o:"sacrifice" o:"search your library for a basic land card"

canon_recall.sample_noise: Also surfaces Dawntreader Elk, Diligent Farmhand — legitimate tech, low noise.

mana_rocks_big.intent: Artifacts that tap to add 2+ colorless mana — the backbone of colorless-heavy decks like eldrazi.

canon_recall.sample_noise: Worn Powerstone, Basalt Monolith, Grim Monolith are legitimate ramp tech; Mana Vault is fast mana (valid in higher brackets). Noise is minimal.

mana_dorks.intent: 1-CMC creature mana producers — ramp that also adds board presence.

canon_recall.sample_noise: Elvish Mystic, Fyndhorn Elves are functional equivalents (correct noise — all valid includes). Delighted Halfling surfaces too (conditional colored mana, legitimate tech).

cheat_into_play.intent: Repeatable or one-shot effects that put creature cards from hand onto the battlefield without paying their mana costs — the payoff for building excess mana.
queries: f:commander o:"put a creature card from your hand onto the battlefield"

canon_recall.sample_noise: Quicksilver Amulet and Monster Manual are legitimate alternatives. Ilharg (attack-trigger version) also surfaces — valid tech. Noise quality is high.

eldrazi_annihilator.intent: Sub-recipe absorbing eldrazi-colorless: game-closing Eldrazi threats with annihilator that justify the ramp investment.

canon_recall.sample_noise: It That Betrays is a legitimate include for blue-adjacent strategies. Ulamog, the Defiler (MH3) also surfaces. All Eldrazi — noise is intentionally on-theme.

eldrazi_apex.intent: Emrakul-tier threats with cast triggers and protection — the highest-ceiling payoffs for ramp decks.

canon_recall.sample_noise: Emrakul, the Aeons Torn is banned in Commander and excluded by f:commander. Minimal noise — only shows legal apex Eldrazi.

wildcard.intent: Intentionally broad — surfaces ramp-adjacent cards (cost reducers, untap effects, mana doublers) that the idiom-specific queries miss. High noise; run sparingly.
queries: f:commander o:"add mana" o:"creatures you control" order:edhrec

canon_recall.note: Wildcard is not validated against canon — it exists to surface new printings and unusual mana producers the precise sub-recipes miss.

runtime_semantics.color_identity_splice: Append `id<=<deck color identity>` per query at runtime.
runtime_semantics.decklist_exclusion: Post-fetch — filter out any name already in decklist or candidates.json top-50.

validation_summary.notes: All 17 canon cards confirmed surfaced by empirical Scryfall API queries. forest_fetch_sorceries uses Scryfall OR-parenthesis syntax `(t:sorcery or t:instant)`; validate at runtime if MCP wrapper doesn't support parentheses — fallback: run as two separate queries split by type.
